outcomes.outcome: This adventure has reached its authored closing event with the actual successes or losses acknowledged. Its earned result and continuing consequences remain true.

failure_conditions: Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.
Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

gm_guidance.instructions:
Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. Give plainly visible facts and essential leads without a roll; success can improve position, speed or discretion. A supported spell or sound equipment use can solve an obstacle outright when its actual text allows. Track the real HP, spell slots, ammunition, carried gear and recovery resources; never restore them between scenes by narration. These Plans do not install extra engine procedures. The encounter profiles below are complete bounded GM adaptations for the stated baseline, not the full Setting stat blocks or certified CR ratings. Use only their listed attacks and traits. All have one action, no multiattack, legendary actions, resistances, immunities or unlisted spellcasting. Ordinary rules for movement, cover, opportunity attacks, surprise and surrender still apply. For an uncertain opposing ability check or save, use the listed modifiers without inventing proficiency. Before engagement, admit the actors through the current encounter tools and declare any supported additional trait. Never narrate a proprietary creature power as an automatic engine effect. Every encounter has a reason to occur and a way to withdraw, negotiate or gain an advantage. Honour a clever bypass as a mechanical success; preserve the wider hazardous adventure instead of forcing a replacement fight. Do not reduce this prepared adventure to a sequence of conversations.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: The player chooses their actions, loyalties and risks. Refusal, failed checks, retreat, scouting, spell use and enemy surrender can change the route. A check resolves an uncertain action, not another person’s entire will.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Baseline: one level-2 Player Character with no Companions. A lower-level or badly depleted solo character should face one active enemy at a time and the reduced HP/damage option stated for the encounter; prepare that adjustment before initiative. For a small adventuring party, add at most one ordinary foe to a fight before it starts, or use an appropriate fully supported profile after inspecting the actual party. Larger parties need deliberate rebalancing. Character compatibility does not enforce level or establish balance. Allied workers supply information, ropes and agreed off-screen work; they never receive free player-character combat turns.
gm_guidance.railroading: Use the authored sites, opposition, clues and consequences. Core clues have alternate routes; opening a door or making a routine observation never chooses the character’s next action. Later acts inherit actual resources, wounds, allies and evidence. Keep stakes local to this expedition, relic, crew or route: the Anchor Door mystery and world-scale climax belong to The Rift Awakening.

facts.fact: Two salvage crews claim the same storehouse after a Hollows district returned in a changed arrangement. The entrance route is occupied by Rift-touched predators.
Both crews will pay toward a 30 gp scouting fee. Each has useful gear, but neither wants to send workers blind into the other’s claim.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

intended_player_experience: A focused Severed Lands D&D adventure combining dangerous exploration, meaningful character abilities and prepared combat with choices about the people involved.

completion_conditions: The survey reaches the storehouse loading court by the braced lintel, roofwalk or low gate, or an ended failed scouting attempt returns to boundary yard A with the blocked approach identified.

The two balcony workers are rescued to the boundary yard or their observed outcomes or last known positions are reported after withdrawal. The crew marks, Lysa's diagram and receipts establish Vennic's incompatible promises; on failed access, record exactly which evidence remains inaccessible rather than asserting it was found.

Closing event: at boundary yard A, Dessa and Orl receive the scouting and worker report and state what equipment or labour they will actually offer for the storehouse haul. If the player declines the haul altogether, end the expedition with this report and keep Act 2 unplayed.

opening_direction: Begin at a marked Hollows boundary with rival foreworkers Dessa and Orl. Show the newly returned storehouse, smoke from a missing survey team’s lamp and both crews’ offers. The player has not chosen a side.
premise: Two crews need the same route into a newly returned Hollows storehouse. Scout a monster-held district, open its dangerous vault and bring the salvage out before their rivalry turns violent.

secrets.fact: Vennic knowingly sold incompatible exclusive access after the district joined the old route to the new stair.

reveal.condition: Compare both receipts, the joined crew marks and Lysa’s dated diagram.

branches: Combine the crews’ equipment, pay for your own safe approach or accept a more difficult unsupported route.
Rescue from the roof, draw the spider away or fight for the square.
consequences: Record workers saved, borrowed gear, actual injuries and the channel found through Investigation.

planned_encounters: Fight 1, a juvenile Rift Phase Spider guarding C. Juvenile phase spider (monstrosity): AC 12, HP 16, speed 30 ft, initiative +2. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 piercing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  This immature adaptation has no planar jaunt, poison burst or paralysis. Its climb movement is used only if admitted; otherwise it uses the accessible rubble ramps. Silk strands are visible terrain, requiring an action to clear or a safe detour, not an automatic restrained condition. It retreats if bloodied and offered prey away from the balcony. Solo level 1: HP 10 and bite 1d4+1.
situations: Cast and truth. Dessa’s Red Hook crew maintained the old route; Orl’s White Ladder crew has a valid claim on a new stair that now joins it. Broker Vennic knowingly promised exclusive access to both. Surveyor Lysa’s dates and two receipts prove the double sale. These facts complicate ownership but do not kill the predators or lift a collapsed gate. Dessa can lend timber, Orl rope and Lysa a survey mark key; fair terms determine what help is genuinely available.

Connected survey site. A boundary yard reaches B collapsed lintel, then C an overgrown square. D roofwalk bypasses C and drops onto E, the storehouse loading court. C also reaches E by a barred low gate. Two workers shelter on a balcony above C after a juvenile Rift Phase Spider occupied the square. The roofwalk offers a safe place to plan, but its last gap needs a fixed rope or Athletics DC 12. An unsupported failed jump lands on the lower awning for 1d6 bludgeoning; a belay prevents the fall.

Opening the way. Inspection shows the lintel’s unstable hinge. A timber brace borrowed from Dessa and a rope from Orl make a controlled lift possible without a roll. A hurried solo lift is Athletics DC 13; failure drops loose chips, Dexterity save DC 12 for 1d4 bludgeoning on failure, no damage on success, and the route remains blocked. The roofwalk is an alternative. The gate has a tools DC 12 lock; a failed attempt costs time while the spider changes position visibly. Lysa’s key opens it without a check. A rescue line from D can take the workers out above the predator if actually anchored.

What the survey proves. Each crew’s mark is visible on a different wall now joined by phasing. One recovered worker carries Lysa’s recent diagram and a receipt dated after the street changed. Comparison exposes Vennic’s incompatible promises without a single crucial die roll. Investigation DC 12 additionally identifies the old safe loading channel through the storehouse, giving an alternate approach next act. Failure leaves the main door available. Returning to A permits a safe short rest and a chance to fetch promised equipment; the local phasing warning will be announced before a dangerous re-entry.

planned_encounters: Fight 2, small Rift Mimic in I. Small Rift Mimic (monstrosity): AC 12, HP 17, speed 15 ft, initiative +0. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 bludgeoning. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  Its imitation is fictional camouflage. This smaller adaptation lacks Adhesive, automatic grappling, acid damage and immunities. A hit does only the declared damage. It follows food and withdraws at 5 HP. The cage bars and pump channel offer ways to contain it with actual actions and movement. Solo level 1: HP 10 and 1d4+1 damage.
situations: Agreement with a purpose. Dessa wants old crew tools returned; Orl needs saleable stock for wages. Before entry, offer a division by marked crates, a pooled sale or a witnessed fee arrangement. A failed Persuasion check cannot turn both into irrational enemies; unsupported promises simply do not secure their extra labour. Vennic’s exposure can recover his fee but does not settle the remaining share. The crews can provide a hauling team only after real terms are agreed.

Storehouse layout. F loading floor connects the main door and the hidden loading channel to G tally room, H pump gallery and I inner salvage cage. G holds a cargo manifest and a release lever for I. H contains a drained channel that can be used as a sheltered approach to the lever. I holds legitimate trade ingots and a false Warden lockbox. A hanging gantry crosses F above two old loading weights. Place both exits clearly; no phase removes them merely because the player prepared a good route.

Trap and treasure choice. A scratched maintenance plate in G explains the loading weights. Investigation DC 12 identifies the sprung plate by I; thieves’ tools DC 13 or a brace from H disables it. Failure triggers Dexterity save DC 12, 1d6 bludgeoning on failure and none on success, then the weight hangs spent. The manifest distinguishes crew tools from 60 gp of saleable ingots. The apparently valuable lockbox is a small Rift Mimic; wet organic seams and a smell of spoiled meat are observable clues. A pole prod from distance, food diversion or opening the cage from H avoids grabbing it. A character who correctly suspects it gains that advantage rather than an arbitrary surprise anyway.

Extraction under pressure. Opening the outer cage produces a visible violet shimmer from the returning district. Explain the warning and remaining route before asking what to carry. The ingots require several loads according to actual carrying limits; workers supplied by the agreement can carry them, while a solo character may secure only the most valuable crate. The secured roofwalk and rescued workers from Act 1 create alternatives. A short rest back at A is possible; returning afterward may require a new survey if the district has visibly phased. This is a disclosed choice, not an unannounced punishment for resting.

Settlement and ending. Divide actual salvaged goods under the agreement; the party receives its 30 gp fee and any explicitly negotiated share. If a crew breaks terms, its tools and witnessed receipt create leverage for arbitration, not mandatory gang warfare. Losing the ingots can still leave rescued workers and an honest route survey worth the scouting payment. Name who can safely use the route and what obligations survive. End with the first completed or abandoned shared haul, not a new regional war.

title: The Scavengers’ Accord
tone: A ruin expedition where tactical cooperation earns a lasting agreement.
unsupported_mechanics: Site phasing, enemy motives, alarms and engineering objectives are explicitly described GM adjudications. Checks, saves, damage, spells, rest and admitted combat use the D&D Ruleset. No extra automatic hazard, pursuit, faction, economy or crafting subsystem is installed.
Listed creature profiles are weaker or specialised Setting adaptations with declared statistics. They do not assert support for unencoded powers from the original monster entries.

Gold and salvage become awarded possessions only when recorded through the applicable inventory/state path. SRD Lite has a reduced spell list (117 supported spells) and no consumables; consumables belong to future SRD Full. A narrative reward never installs a magic-item feature, restores a slot or applies healing.
